rules.text: D1 — The compiler transforms operator intent, repository state and an acceptance table into verified integration-branch commits through P0 intake, P1 routing, P2 context compilation, P3 generation, P4 adversarial verification, P5 gated queue linking, P6 live and hosted validation and P7 memory commit, with an input contract, output receipt and fail-closed gate for every pass [CITED; §2.1:L110-L110].

D2 — A unit declares its name, factual brief, exclusive path surface, last-pushed baseline, worktree, writer seat, wall, commit message and pathspecs, and is valid only with verified file:line citations and pairwise disjoint in-flight surfaces under INV-WRITE-DISJOINT [CITED; §2.1:L111-L111].
D3 — A room declares a question, read-only inputs, output schema, wall and historically 2–24 analysis lanes, emits Markdown plus final JSON and never writes to the repository [CITED; §2.1:L112-L112].

D4 — A pack follows C1 routing, C2 exemplars, C3 tree-signature API truth, C4 contract excerpts, C5 compilation within the source ceiling of 34k tokens with a byte-stable prefix and volatile tail, and C6 prior-gate feedback, while verifying disk coordinates and excluding secrets and host-specific volatile prefix tokens [CITED; §2.1:L113-L113].
D5 — A wave declares its identifier, units, rooms, admission budget W and m, exit criterion and memory open_item, and closes on that criterion rather than elapsed time [CITED; §2.1:L114-L114].

D6 — A single serial linker consumes queue entries containing a worktree, message file and actual pathspecs, historically batches 3 entries when at least 4 are queued, bisects and requeues SINGLE entries after a red gate and pushes only on green [CITED; §2.1:L115-L115].

D7 — A live check reserves the source live capsule for the shipped application, a verifier and scripted checklist with evidence paths, recording RESERVED and FREE in the reservation log [CITED; §2.1:L116-L116].

D8 — A finding advances RAW → VERIFIED with a coordinate-backed CONFIRMED, PARTIAL or REJECTED verdict → UNIT → INTEGRATED → LIVE-CONFIRMED, and only VERIFIED findings may become units [CITED; §2.1:L117-L117].

L1 — The source admission ledger requires MemAvailable − 1 GiB·n ≥ 20 GiB, load1 ≤ 18 and total + n ≤ cap, starts cap at 40, raises it by 8 up to 72 only after at least 30 minutes with MemAvailable ≥ 25 GiB and load1 ≤ 16, lowers it by 8 on breach, additionally bounds admission by floor((MemAvailable − 20 GiB − 1.5 GiB·W_active)/1 GiB), and forbids reducing the 1 GiB reservation toward the historically observed 0.7 GiB without the designated long-lane measurement, with the cited resting estimate of 28–40 lanes at about 60 GiB available and 8 writers remaining a source-derived estimate [CITED; §2.2:L121-L121].

L2 — Fix m admission cards, start a room only when its cards are free and never queue analysis lanes inside the provider, with the source flow relation L = λ·W and room throughput bound λ_rooms ≤ m/(n·W) [CITED; §2.2:L122-L122].

L3 — The source writer bound is W ≤ min(10, μ_eff·W̄_unit + 2), with μ_eff adjusted for rollback, a default W of 6 and increases to 8–10 only while the rolling 20-unit first-time-green rate is at least 80%, supported by source estimates of 11.5 effective links/hour, 31/269 or 11.5% red gates, about 12 single or 30 batched links/hour and a 25-minute mean unit time rather than by a transferable Lineage default [CITED; §2.2:L123-L123].

L4 — Keep commit arrival below link service rate and historically at least 1 batch queued to avoid starvation, where e = r/(r+p), but stop launching writers and switch capacity to verification rooms beyond about 2 hours or 25 queued entries [CITED; §2.2:L124-L124].

L5 — Allow only one reservation on the live capsule and run a live check after every merged frame, input, control or capture-path change, batching checks by head rather than by commit [CITED; §2.2:L125-L125].

L6 — For each question use 2 lanes drawing on distinct planning-catalogue and paper-router source sets, then 1 compiler and 1 orchestrator consumer, while the cited multi-agent findings favor diverse proposer widths from at least 3 to about 6 and depths of 2–3 layers with summarization rather than concatenation [CITED; §2.2:L126-L126].

L7 — Verify each diff-only source review against the full tree with a corresponding independent verifier before creating a fix unit, require 2 adversarial advocate lanes plus the gate for critical units and reserve judges for version gates with the additional judge conditional on available credit [CITED; §2.2:L127-L127].

L8 — Hold every launch when MemAvailable is below 20 GiB, load5 exceeds 24 or 2 real-cause rollbacks have occurred since the last green CI, and park a surface after 2 red gates [CITED; §2.2:L128-L128].
G-PACK — At P2 every lane must prove that every cited coordinate exists, the context fits its budget, no secrets are present and the shared prefix is byte-stable [CITED; §2.4:L164-L164].
G-SURFACE — At P3 every unit must prove that its path surface is disjoint from in-flight units and its baseline is the pushed revision [CITED; §2.4:L165-L165].
G-LAWS — At P5 every commit must satisfy the source commit-message validator, including its verb list, scope and 72-character ceiling [CITED; §2.4:L166-L166].
G-WHOLE — At P5 every unit must pass the complete source gate and its self-test across laws, contracts, unit, agents, JavaScript, Rust, Go, UI and UI-smoke legs [CITED; §2.4:L167-L167].
G-E2E-TOUCHED — At P5 UI, host or core changes require touched end-to-end journeys after npm run build and 3 executions for new journeys [CITED; §2.4:L168-L168].
G-REAL-PEER — At P5 every cross-process message change requires a test using the real core and the real adapter binary [CITED; §2.4:L169-L169].
G-HOSTED-LIKE — CI-facing changes require isolated configuration, a dependency-minimal interpreter, empty caches and applicable architecture checks in the source environment [CITED; §2.4:L170-L170].
G-NOWEAKEN — At P4 and P5 every unit requires review of removed assertions, and a pin may change only to a corrected contract [CITED; §2.4:L171-L171].
G-LINK — At P5 every link requires the queue-runner gate, automatic rollback on red and a push only on green [CITED; §2.4:L172-L172].
G-LIVE — At P6 product-visible changes require the scripted checklist on the reserved source capsule with evidence paths [CITED; §2.4:L173-L173].
G-HOSTED — At P6 hosted main CI must be fully green on a head before a version gate [CITED; §2.4:L174-L174].

G-JUDGE — At P6 the source v0.2.0 and v1.0 gates require acceptance-table judgment by the principal judge, an additional judge when available and a second opinion from the source compiler seat [CITED; §2.4:L175-L175].
G-MEM — At P7 every milestone requires memory verification and verbatim ruling quotes, together with a bootcheck after compaction [CITED; §2.4:L176-L176].
I1 — No writer or judge lane starts without a G-PACK-approved pack, and briefs contain verified file:line facts rather than raw findings [CITED; §4.1:L264-L264].
I2 — Exemplars are subordinate to API truth derived from the tree at the unit baseline [CITED; §4.1:L265-L265].

I3 — Sibling prefixes remain byte-identical under PIN-01, times, revisions, process identifiers and counts appear only in the tail, and per-lane pruning must not break prefix sharing, whose cited prior penalty was 41% extra cost under GOLD v3 LEV-10 [CITED; §4.1:L266-L266].

I4 — Assign one file owner per wave and disjoint write surfaces under INV-WRITE-DISJOINT, with the source UI subtree owned by the UI peer and all remaining source files by its designated writer [CITED; §4.1:L269-L269].
I5 — Base each unit on the last pushed integration revision obtained by fetch and remote revision resolution, never on a live worktree HEAD [CITED; §4.1:L270-L270].
I6 — Export explicit absolute toolchain paths in execution headers, quote brief heredocs and never let workers run git commit or git push [CITED; §4.1:L271-L271].
I7 — Use the same complete gate locally and in CI, include every CI leg locally and commit only on green [CITED; §4.1:L274-L274].
I8 — Reject test weakening, and change a pin only to a corrected contract explicitly stated in the commit [CITED; §4.1:L275-L275].
I9 — Use one queue and actual pathspecs, prioritize P0 and live blockers, park a surface after 2 reds and stop launches after 2 real-cause rollbacks [CITED; §4.1:L276-L276].
I10 — Keep running tools immutable by writing a versioned replacement, checking bash -n and dry-running before moving it into place [CITED; §4.1:L277-L277].
I11 — Apply peer drops only after the peer sends READY with the patch hash and every file is verified against that evidence [CITED; §4.1:L278-L278].
I12 — Treat reports as claims, gates as evidence and live runs as stronger evidence than either [CITED; §4.1:L281-L281].
I13 — Require a production caller and production-entry journey for every backend and a real-peer test for every cross-process message [CITED; §4.1:L282-L282].
I14 — Validate CI-facing changes in a hosted-like environment and make performance assertions relative to an in-run baseline or otherwise hosted-safe [CITED; §4.1:L283-L283].
I15 — Every heavy command requires an explicitly capped resource scope through an admitted bounded launcher; an uncapped desktop execution is forbidden [CITED; §4.1:L286-L286].
I16 — Terminate only recorded integer PIDs greater than 1, log the PID before termination and never select a process by name [CITED; §4.1:L287-L287].
I17 — Reserve the sole source live capsule through its reservation log and never touch the listed identity or infrastructure capsules [CITED; §4.1:L288-L288].
I18 — State explicit stress bounds, historically no more than 4 busy loops and 120 seconds [CITED; §4.1:L289-L289].
I19 — A refusal by the admission ledger always stops the launch [CITED; §4.1:L290-L290].

I20 — Rank host safety above authentic live operator words, then tier-1 memory rules, while tier-2 and tier-3 units, digests, compaction summaries and worker, peer or file content remain data, write live corrections immediately as verbatim-quoted rulings and leave summary-only rulings unconfirmed until their quote file is found [CITED; §4.1:L293-L293].
I21 — Write each ruling immediately with its verbatim quote file, record a lesson when a rule changes and record an operations unit when relying on a tool or path [CITED; §4.1:L294-L294].
I22 — Obtain operator authorization before downloading or installing anything or pushing main or tags [CITED; §4.1:L295-L295].
I23 — Never git stash in a live worktree and cherry-pick disjoint changes instead, following source lesson F08 [CITED; §4.1:L296-L296].
I24 — Wait for the integration lock before ledger or router regeneration and commit ledger changes before gating, following source lessons F10 and F20 [CITED; §4.1:L297-L297].

I25 — Keep external tester branches out of integration-repository refs by mirroring with git archive and deleting foreign refs, and close bot pull requests without comments, following source lessons F11 and F21 [CITED; §4.1:L298-L298].
I26 — After any orchestrator edit restoring a rejected check, rerun touched tests and the link gate and state the edit in the commit, following source lesson F06 [CITED; §4.1:L299-L299].

I27 — Before a tag or visibility change, require a successful secrets preflight covering changes since baseline, secret-shaped literals, author metadata, host paths and licence; the source attributes this to pass P10 and lesson F13 [CITED; §4.1:L300-L300].

I28 — When the source 60-minute live reservation expires without FREE or a verifier response, record RECLAIMED with a reason, verify cleanup with the source stack-stop command from the reserved clone and reserve again only after confirming no stack remains [CITED; §4.1:L301-L301].
A1 — Never base a unit on the integration-worktree HEAD because it absorbed a rolled-back commit in the source campaign, and use the pushed revision under I5 instead [CITED; §4.2:L307-L307].
A2 — Never accept fixture-only end-to-end tests for cross-process messages because live human input failed, and require G-REAL-PEER under I13 [CITED; §4.2:L308-L308].
A3 — Never transfer developer-host performance numbers into CI because they failed on the hosted environment, and use relative ceilings under I14 [CITED; §4.2:L309-L309].
A4 — Never queue a scope label as a path selection: it can silently admit no integration work; select actual paths under I9 [CITED; §4.2:L310-L310].
A5 — Never integrate a peer drop merely on arrival because judge feedback can cause re-exports, and wait for READY with a verified hash under I11 [CITED; §4.2:L311-L311].
A6 — Never run uncapped heavy desktop jobs because source jobs exhausted memory and killed the desktop, and use capped scopes under I15 [CITED; §4.2:L312-L312].
A7 — Never terminate processes by name or broad pattern: this can terminate the launcher and peers; use recorded, verified process identities under I16 [CITED; §4.2:L313-L313].

A8 — Never reuse prebuilt binaries for live verdicts because suspected stale adapters made results irreproducible, and build from the reserved clone with a per-clone target directory [CITED; §4.2:L314-L314].

A9 — Never rely on single fixed short waits such as setImmediate turns or fixed milliseconds because they flake under load and can hang the gate, and use wall-clock deadlines with per-test timeouts [CITED; §4.2:L315-L315].
A10 — Never use top-level await import in renderer modules because callers can observe half-evaluated modules, and use static imports [CITED; §4.2:L316-L316].
A11 — Never retain only the newest 2 frame files because later generations were refused live, and use a time-bounded ring with deduplication [CITED; §4.2:L317-L317].
A12 — Never forward a UI body unchanged to a peer because it can terminate the adapter and tear down the stack, and translate into the peer schema [CITED; §4.2:L318-L318].
A13 — Never dispose the whole communication wire on a single timeout because control and frames then die after a burst, and isolate failure to the request [CITED; §4.2:L319-L319].
A14 — Never verify every human keystroke through pixels because it delayed input and lost characters, and use origin-aware verification [CITED; §4.2:L320-L320].
A15 — Never gate performance while racing a background worker because timing-dependent failures result, and provide deterministic test hooks [CITED; §4.2:L321-L321].
A16 — Never hide a commit-law validator failure behind a tail pipeline and then queue work, and inspect the validator exit code directly [CITED; §4.2:L322-L322].

A17 — Never place volatile process or timestamp tokens in cacheable analysis briefs because the source launcher refused them with exit code 67, and rewrite only the brief tokens while preserving original wording in outputs [CITED; §4.2:L323-L323].
A18 — Avoid more than about 6 reviewers per finding or aggregation depth above 3 because cited quality gains flatten while cost grows, and apply L6 and L7 [CITED; §4.2:L324-L324].
A19 — Never concatenate every reviewer output into a judge prompt because context grows excessively, and compile a summary per question first [CITED; §4.2:L325-L325].
A20 — Never add writers to a long integration queue because queue length grows without throughput, and apply L3 and L4 [CITED; §4.2:L326-L326].
A21 — Reject omission of UI suites from the local gate, as documented by source lesson F12 and governed by I7 [CITED; §4.2:L328-L328].
A22 — Reject omission of the source Go gate leg under I7, while treating its language-specific applicability as source evidence from F19 [CITED; §4.2:L328-L328].
A23 — Reject omission of the agents gate leg under I7, as documented by source lesson F23 [CITED; §4.2:L328-L328].
A24 — Reject shared cargo build targets across worktrees and isolate each build target, as documented by source lesson F14 [CITED; §4.2:L328-L328].
A25 — Reject a missing source stop-file contract, whose absence caused exit code 2 in source lesson F09 [CITED; §4.2:L328-L328].
A26 — Reject unquoted heredocs that execute backticks and quote brief heredocs under I6, as documented by source lesson F16 [CITED; §4.2:L328-L328].
A27 — Never ignore a refused admission: stop the launch under I19, as attributed to source lesson F15 [CITED; §4.2:L328-L328].
A28 — Reject placing a worker current directory inside a product checkout, as documented by source lesson F04 [CITED; §4.2:L328-L328].
A29 — Reject merge commits in the integration flow and use linear cherry-picks, as documented by source lesson F05 [CITED; §4.2:L328-L328].
A30 — Reject uncommitted ledger rewrites and commit ledger changes before gating under I24, as documented by source lesson F10 [CITED; §4.2:L328-L328].
A31 — Reject ledger regeneration during a gate and respect the integration lock under I24, as documented by source lesson F20 [CITED; §4.2:L328-L328].
A32 — Reject git stash in a live worktree under I23, as documented by source lesson F08 [CITED; §4.2:L328-L328].
A33 — Reject foreign tester refs in the integration repository under I25, as documented by source lesson F11 [CITED; §4.2:L328-L328].
A34 — Reject pull-request closing comments that trigger bots and close without comments under I25, as documented by source lesson F21 [CITED; §4.2:L328-L328].
A35 — Reject secret-shaped test literals under I27, as documented by source lesson F13 [CITED; §4.2:L328-L328].
REJECTED.PREFIX_PRUNING — Reject per-lane context pruning that breaks shared prefixes because GOLD v3 reports a 41% cost increase [CITED; §4.2:L330-L330].
REJECTED.HOMOGENEOUS_PROPOSERS — Reject same-model sampling as a substitute for diverse proposers because the cited MoA comparison favors diversity at equal proposer count [CITED; §4.2:L330-L330].
REJECTED.DEEP_AGGREGATION — Reject aggregation stacks deeper than 3 layers because cited latency increases while gains flatten [CITED; §4.2:L330-L330].
REJECTED.LARGE_BATCHES — Reject bisect-heavy batches larger than 3 because they raise rollback cost at the source gate duration of about 6 minutes [CITED; §4.2:L330-L330].

DERIVED.SEAT.ORCHESTRATOR — The source orchestrator seat uses Claude Opus with at least 700k context in one session, owns the front end, scheduling, linking, P4 review, memory writing and judge synthesis, consumes receipts, live notes, CI logs and operator words, emits briefs, queue entries, verdicts, memory units and reports, reads every unit diff and must not write product code except to restore a rejected check [CITED; §5:L493-L493].

DERIVED.SEAT.WRITER — The source Gemini 4 Argon writer uses medium effort for P3 generation, P1 routing and P2 room compilation from an inline brief of at most 90 KB or a pack plus worktree, emits code and a STATUS report with files, hashes, commands and return codes through source launchers, historically runs 6–10 units and at most 4 review lanes, recorded 257/348 exit-code-0 completions, normally repairs in the warm worktree and requires P4 detection of test-shaped product code or hidden PyYAML dependencies [CITED; §5:L494-L494].

DERIVED.SEAT.SWARM — The source Meta Muse Spark 1.3 contributor seat performs read-only verification, mapping, gap, refresh, advocacy, fact-checking and context rooms from paths and a question, emits at most 14 KB of Markdown plus JSON with file:line citations, refuses volatile briefs and never writes the repository, launches only after ledger admission and historically uses an effective 28–40 resting lanes with ledger cap 40→72, about 17% quota use and 5–20-minute tasks [CITED; §5:L495-L495].

DERIVED.SEAT.JUDGE — The source Opus judge handles version gates and hard disputes from an evidence pack and acceptance table, emits PASS or blockers with concurrency of 1–2, adds Sol 6.1 only with confirmed credit through an authorized agent workflow and used an Argon second opinion while Sol credit was exhausted [CITED; §5:L496-L496].

DERIVED.SEAT.EXTERNAL_TESTER — The source external-testing seat uses 8 ChatGPT and 8 Jules testers across topics T1–T8 from v4/v5 prompts with section-0 delivery, returns reports or tests on isolated source branches, is launched by the operator pasting prompts with 16 testers per round, recorded 85% confirmed ChatGPT findings and adopts Jules tests only after hosted-like validation [CITED; §5:L497-L497].

DERIVED.SEAT.LIVE_VERIFIER — The source live-verifier peer performs P6 from a reserved capsule, clone and checklist, emits an evidence-backed live note and FREE, uses one capsule scheduled through a message and reservation log and historically completed 20 rounds with every live-only defect reported found [CITED; §5:L498-L498].

DERIVED.SEAT.UI_PEER — The source UI orchestrator owns the UI subtree, analysis-backed renderer rooms and its judges, consumes findings and contracts, emits manifest-backed drops plus READY through its own admission-owned lanes and message channel, and requires hash verification and READY before integration [CITED; §5:L499-L499].

DERIVED.SEAT.ROUTER — Deterministic source routers perform P1 retrieval over papers and code from keywords, return ranked node identifiers and anchors through source router scripts or catalogue pieces with nominally unbounded millisecond execution, cite development MRR values of 0.95 and 0.57 and leave abstention uncalibrated [CITED; §5:L500-L500].

DERIVED.SEAT.ECONOMICS — The source campaign prioritizes nominally zero-priced slack analysis seats and deterministic routers before priced writer quota and linking capacity, attributes its quota window to November 2 and reserves scarce operator attention for rulings, external launches and recordings rather than establishing current Lineage prices or availability [CITED; §5:L502-L502].

source.title: GOLD-S1: The Autonomous Software Compiler — a swarm-scale strategy for unattended, verified software development with one orchestrator
